ledger.note: 29 May 1557: Philip II fixes the Presidi. 'On 29 May 1557, Philip signed a treaty in London with Lord Iacopo VI Appiani of Piombino'; the state 'existed between 1557 and 1801'. The land is the Tuscan coast fortresses the Siena page lists as successors.

1708: the Austrian Habsburgs hold the Presidi through their viceroy in Naples ('1708-1733: Austrian Habsburgs, administered by their viceroy in Naples'); before it was the Spanish Crown, 'administered by the Spanish Habsburg viceroy of Naples' from 1557.

May 1735: the Presidi pass to Don Carlos. 'During the subsequent War of the Polish Succession in May 1735, a Spanish and allied army under the Duke of Montemar' took them; the Treaty of Turin (26 September 1733) had promised them to Don Carlos 'together with the kingdoms of Naples and Sicily', the emperor's diploma ceding them is dated 11 December 1736 and the Peace of Vienna of 18 November 1738 made it definitive. 1735-1801: Spanish Bourbon kings of Naples. [Reviewer eu-13-x, 2026-10-31: moved from 26 September 1733 (the treaty promise) to the conquest of May 1735 on the same page, matching habsburg-monarchy /ledger/70 and kingdom-of-naples-bourbon /ledger/1.]

notes: A colony-type dossier, written from one full page and the Siena infobox. The Presidi were administered from Naples (Spanish and Austrian viceroys, then Bourbon kings); the suzerain relation belongs to the kingdom-of-spain / habsburg-monarchy / kingdom-of-naples-bourbon dossiers, which do not record it. Unsettled: the Presidi's boundaries (circles of 10 and 6 km are readings), Giannutri islet, the start date within 1555-1557 (Spanish troops held the coast from 1555; the Kingdom of Naples page gives the Treaty of London of 1557 and calls the cities 'part of the Kingdom of Naples'), and the 1736-1738 steps of the Bourbon cession. Gazetteer names: none (coordinates).
